explanation: The Campaign of Porto Calvo article, § Background, puts the campaign at the end of a sequence it starts at Bahia: "the year 1624 saw the Dutch fleet arriving off the coast of Salvador, where a swift invasion ensued, resulting in the city’s capture within a remarkably brief span of 24 hours. This marked an acceleration of their territorial expansion in Brazil", and then, of the campaign itself, that John Maurice, governor from 1636, "spearheaded multiple far-reaching expeditions aimed at further territorial growth and consolidation". The type `enabled` is what the article’s own wording carries. The 1624 capture is what it says the expansion accelerated from, thirteen years before this campaign, and the article gives it as no cause of this campaign in particular. Probable: Wikipedia alone, at two revisions. The article attributes the passage to Clemmy Manzo, The Rough Guide to Brazil (2014) and to Erik Odegard, Patronage, Patrimonialism, and Governors’ Careers in the Dutch Chartered Companies, 1630–1681 (2022), pp. 60–62. Wikipedia itself cites those works, and review A2 would allow one of them as a second author. Nobody read either here, so the edge stays probable.
